clue.text: Type of bowling that's not on leg!

definitions.text: Type of bowling that's not on leg!

parts.words: Type of bowling that's not on leg!
parts.note: a cricket ball can be delivered with the hand kept low, beneath the shoulder; the joke is that it is done under an arm rather than a leg

explanation.surface: A cricket coach describes a style of delivery that has nothing to do with the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'leg' is a side of the field (leg side). Here it is read literally: this delivery happens below an arm, not a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bowling with the hand released below shoulder height is the low-armed style, an old-fashioned delivery.

clue.text: Lops head off flower

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or not right, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener cuts the top off a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram of LOPS HEAD. The surface makes 'Lops head off' a gardening action.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family plant with white or yellow blooms, famed in Greek myth.

clue.text: Apres-ski, maybe when it's less expensive?

definitions.meaning: after skiing you come down from the mountain top, away from the summit
travel or power used outside busy hours is charged at a cheaper rate

explanation.surface: Wondering whether after-ski drinks are cheaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Outside rush hours, tickets and electricity are sold at lower tariffs; and literally it means away from the summit.

clue.text: Engineers wrong to answer back

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Engineers who are in the wrong talk back.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp reply, and as a verb it means to reply quickly or wittily.

clue.text: For him, work is a grind

definitions.text: For him, work is a grind

parts.words: For him, work is a grind
parts.note: someone who runs a mill literally grinds corn for a living, so the weary phrase is true to the letter

explanation.surface: A complaint about a man who finds his job tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who operates a flour mill grinds grain all day, so his trade is literally grinding.

clue.text: Patient's protracted agony

parts.note: drawn out in time, lengthy
great pain or distress

explanation.surface: A hospital patient endures drawn-out pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like a noun for a sick person, but it is the adjective meaning enduring without complaint; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bears trouble without complaining for a long time shows great patience.

clue.text: Nerd is in Shakespearean character on course, moving student

indicators.note: the swot is placed inside the pair of words that follow
in a down clue the king's name sits on top of the watercourse

parts.note: Lear is the king of Shakespeare's tragedy
a river follows a course, the watercourse itself
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geek appears as a Shakespeare character on a course, studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' places the swot between the king and the course. The definition is witty: a pupil learning to drive is a student on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone being taught to drive a car is a pupil who is literally in motion while learning.

clue.text: In decline, how long idling untidily?

indicators.note: untidy suggests a mess, so the letters of the three words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking how long someone has been lazing about messily while their life slides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidily' signals the anagram of HOW LONG IDLING, all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for deteriorating steadily pictures a slide down a slope.

clue.text: Man's great upset before reaching hospital

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come first, then the next piece is reached
upset means overturned or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: A man is badly shaken before he gets to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GREAT into GARET; the 's of 'Man's' is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gareth is a man's given name, common in Wales.

clue.text: Cry aloud for one in shellfish's grip

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the numeral is put inside the shellfish
the shellfish holds the numeral in its grip, enclosing it

parts.note: a clam is a bivalve shellfish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone shouts in support of a person caught in a shellfish's clutches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cry aloud' is the definition, not a sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce something publicly and loudly is to declare it officially.

clue.text: Regularly sourced raw material

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Mining output obtained on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: From s-O-u-R-c-E-d take the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock mined for its metal is the raw material from which metals are smelted.

clue.text: You should set down in lake and away from the sea

parts.note: taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to land on a lake when far from the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You should set down' is an instruction to write the next words out in turn, with lake shortened to its map letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Places located in the interior of a country, distant from the coast, are described this way.

clue.text: Later, slightly confused, say nothing for close friend

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
eg (for example) is how 'say' introduces an example
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Later, a bit muddled, keep quiet about a best friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly confused' turns LATER into ALTER; 'say' gives EG and 'nothing' O.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'other self', it is used for a trusted intimate companion as well as a second personality.

clue.text: When one expects a letter from Crete?

definitions.meaning: short for estimated time of arrival, the time someone is expected
Crete is Greek, and this is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: When will a letter from a Greek island arrive?
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests post, but it is an alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: It abbreviates estimated time of arrival, and is also a Greek alphabet character.

clue.text: Book hike in bush

parts.note: a ramble is a long walk in the country

explanation.surface: Arranging a walk through the countryside scrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny shrub, the blackberry plant, is a common hedgerow bush.

clue.text: Public transport isn't quite bankrupt

indicators.note: not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bust means broke, insolvent

explanation.surface: The public transport company is nearly broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A large road vehicle carrying paying passengers is the commonest form of public transport.

clue.text: Bird from Sweden going to bask

indicators.note: the country's letter is followed by the next piece

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
to wallow is to indulge or lie luxuriating, as one basks

explanation.surface: A bird from Sweden flies off to soak up the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A fork-tailed migratory songbird known for summer arrivals in Europe.

clue.text: Game birds — or wolf, possibly?

parts.note: read the answer's second word as a jumble and the first as its signal: a wild version of those four letters spells wolf

explanation.surface: Asking whether game birds might instead be a wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as 'wild' (an anagram signal) applied to FOWL, would give WOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks, geese and other birds hunted for sport are collectively called this.

clue.text: Ill-balanced poles did topple

indicators.note: to topple is to fall over, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Unsteady poles fell over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topple' signals the anagram of POLES DID.
explanation.definitionFit: Something leaning more to one side than the other is lacking in balance.

clue.text: Fellow almost trapping spy — a kind of red

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes
the man holds the spy inside him

parts.note: a fellow is a man
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A man nearly catches a spy, with a red tint mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapping' gives MAGENTAN, the fellow around the spy; 'almost' then cuts its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A purplish-crimson shade, named after a battle in Italy, counted as a red.

clue.text: Exotic scarab is in plant

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters are transformed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A foreign beetle is found in a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic' signals the anagram of SCARAB IS.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabbage genus, including kale, broccoli and turnips, is a plant group.

clue.text: I won't visit grave containing watery liquid

indicators.note: if the letter will not call, it is absent from the word

parts.note: grave means solemn, weighty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declines to visit a tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective meaning solemn.
explanation.definitionFit: In physiology the adjective describes fluids like serum and membranes that produce a thin fluid.

clue.text: Had a good press?

parts.note: newspaper praise is a good press, but clothing passed under a hot iron has also had a good press

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone received favourable newspaper coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes smoothed with a hot flat appliance have been pressed.

clue.text: Beastly bloomer needs earth

indicators.note: the flower requires the next letter after it

parts.note: a bloomer is something that blooms; the lupin is a garden flower
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A flowering plant must have soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder or a loaf, but here it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means wolfish, like a wild animal, so beastly in the literal sense.

clue.text: Atlas, perhaps, setters ent back

indicators.note: sent back means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the words are run together as held; read as 'setter sent', a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Atlas, maybe, was sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held runs 'setter sent' together as 'setters ent'. A setter is a gundog, and sending it back reverses its three-letter name.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas was a Titan of Greek myth who held up the heavens, a deity.

clue.text: Implication concerning way of speaking

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a dispute over money
tone is the manner or quality of voice

explanation.surface: A remark about how someone talks.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertone of suggestion beyond the literal meaning is an implied sense.

clue.text: Frozen stiff in fine outfit shown by papers

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil leads
a rig is a set of clothes, a get-up
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Someone frozen to the bone in a smart costume, as the newspapers show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' suggests newspapers but means identity documents.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means intensely cold, as when someone is chilled to the bone.

clue.text: Money-spinner?

parts.note: a profitable venture is a money-spinner, but this casino device literally spins while money is staked on it

explanation.surface: A remark about a highly profitable business.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating casino device with numbered pockets turns as gamblers bet cash.
